complex.name: CompLex 2.0 / SemEval 2021 Task 1

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.scope: Dataset text and numeric ratings; excludes third-party article/reading-material full texts.

field_descriptions.target_token: Word or multiword expression to assess.
field_descriptions.corpus: Source domain: bible, biomed or europarl.
field_descriptions.expression_type: single for a single word, multi for a multiword expression.

complex.text_policy: Original selected text and capitalization preserved byte-for-byte after UTF-8/CSV decoding; grouping uses a separate whitespace-normalized casefolded hash. No spelling correction, truncation, label imputation, or score transformation.
complex.grouping_rule: Connected components of casefolded target tokens and whitespace-normalized casefolded sentences, spanning both expression types. Group IDs do not alter official splits.
complex.split_policy: Official train retained; official trial mapped to validation; labelled test retained as test. Connected groups or exact inputs crossing official partitions are flagged. For a strict grouped evaluation, assign entire groups jointly before fitting; never use row order as a feature.
complex.source_citation: Shardlow et al. (2021), SemEval-2021 Task 1: Lexical Complexity Prediction, https://aclanthology.org/2021.semeval-1.1/
quality_findings: Sentence-level deduplication would discard distinct lexical targets and is not performed.
TSV is parsed without CSV quote handling: quotation marks in sentences are literal source text.
Trial uses column subcorpus; train/test use corpus. Both are mapped to input.corpus without changing their values.
Original file order can reflect complexity; source row and ID are provenance only.
Crowd-averaged Likert ratings are continuous on the published 0-1 scale.

checks: All retained labels finite and within documented rating scale
Every retained input and label compared with its original decoded CSV/TSV row
Every source row accounted for; invalid/missing labels never imputed
Explicit input allowlists exclude source IDs, other scores, bins, demographics and article full texts
Official splits retained; cross-split identical inputs and connected groups counted and flagged
Source version, downloaded bytes and SHA256 recorded

complex.deduplication_rule: Same task, normalized input, normalized label AND official split; preserve all source_refs. Across-split copies retained and flagged, same-input dependencies unioned. Different labels retained.
complex.sample_id_rule: sha256([task_id,input_hash,label,split]) first 24 hex; official split included to preserve split occurrences.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.scope: Dataset text and numeric ratings; excludes third-party article/reading-material full texts.

field_descriptions.essay: Original English reaction essay written after reading a news story; the news article itself is not included.

empathy.text_policy: Original selected text and capitalization preserved byte-for-byte after UTF-8/CSV decoding; grouping uses a separate whitespace-normalized casefolded hash. No spelling correction, truncation, label imputation, or score transformation.
empathy.grouping_rule: Connected components of source response_id and whitespace-normalized casefolded essay. response_id is a questionnaire response/session key, not a verified permanent participant identifier. Both targets share the same group.
empathy.split_policy: No new fixed split imposed. Future splits must hold out entire groups jointly across both targets. Repeated article IDs are preserved in source_refs for a separate article-disjoint evaluation; response grouping alone does not enforce article independence.

quality_findings: Two separately supervised tasks are generated from each valid reaction; the other target and binary label fields are always excluded from input.
Labels measure the writer self-reported state and are not an objective external measure of empathy.
Only reaction essays are redistributed; no news articles fetched.

asap2.name: ASAP 2.0 (essay and assignment only)

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.scope: Dataset text and numeric ratings; excludes third-party article/reading-material full texts.

field_descriptions.prompt_name: Original assignment topic/title, not an essay or student identifier.
field_descriptions.assignment: Original short assignment instructions if available; null means the source literal NA/empty, never inferred.
field_descriptions.essay: Original student essay. Third-party source reading materials are excluded.

asap2.text_policy: Original selected text and capitalization preserved byte-for-byte after UTF-8/CSV decoding; grouping uses a separate whitespace-normalized casefolded hash. No spelling correction, truncation, label imputation, or score transformation.
asap2.grouping_rule: Whitespace-normalized casefolded essay text hashes. Source essay IDs are unique but are not student IDs; student-disjointness cannot be established. For prompt transfer, hold out whole prompt_name topics in a separate evaluation.
asap2.split_policy: Official train/test assignments preserved exactly. No official validation partition is provided; derive any validation split within train only, retaining connected groups. Exact/normalized duplicates across official splits are flagged, not silently reassigned.
asap2.source_citation: Crossley et al., ASAP 2.0 corpus; repository https://github.com/scrosseye/ASAP_2.0 ; paper https://zenodo.org/records/14781349
asap2.known_cross_dataset_overlap: Publisher states that a substantial subset comes from PERSUADE 2.0. Do not treat PERSUADE and ASAP2 as independent sources in future joint splits; compare original essay identity/text first.
quality_findings: The pinned archives contain 24,728 rows (17,307 train and 7,421 test); README states 24,278 and component counts sum to 24,700. File counts take precedence in this release.
Labels are six ordered integer scores, not genuinely continuous measurements.
All seven prompts have short assignment instructions in some rows; 28 individual rows across five prompts have literal NA, preserved as null without filling from another essay.

No third-party reading-material ZIP was downloaded or published. This is an essay/assignment-only score prediction variant; source-evidence faithfulness cannot be fully evaluated without reading materials.
No student IDs are exposed by the source schema; essay IDs cannot prove student-disjointness.

freesolv.name: FreeSolv experimental hydration free energy

field_descriptions.smiles: RDKit canonical isomeric SMILES; no target-derived properties or experimental uncertainty are input.

freesolv.split_policy: Unassigned. Use scaffold groups for held-out chemical families; the 320-member acyclic group makes folds highly imbalanced. Do not claim a balanced scaffold benchmark.
freesolv.missing_policy: No labels are imputed. Only complete supported structures and finite observed source labels are emitted.
freesolv.precision_policy: Candidate keeps parsed source numbers. Release formatter caps all numeric values at 12 significant digits.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.evidence: README.md License section and LICENSE at the frozen source commit.
license.caveat: Upstream authors license their rights under CC BY 4.0; any original third-party licensing restrictions remain applicable.

quality_findings: 642 finite experimental labels; no molecular identity duplicates after RDKit canonicalization.
Calculated free energy and all uncertainty/reference fields are excluded from input.
Uncertainty values are preserved only as provenance; source defaults are explicitly flagged.
Scaffold grouping is conservative: all acyclic compounds form one large group, and chirality is ignored for grouping.
freesolv.source_citation: Mobley DL and Guthrie JP. FreeSolv: a database of experimental and calculated hydration free energies, with input files. J Comput Aided Mol Des (2014). https://doi.org/10.1007/s10822-014-9747-x
freesolv.grouping_rule: RDKit Bemis-Murcko scaffold without chirality; all acyclic molecules share the empty-scaffold group. Canonical isomeric SMILES identify molecules.

gb1.name: Wu 2016 GB1 four-site observed binding fitness

field_descriptions.residues_at_positions_39_40_41_54: Four standard amino-acid one-letter codes in that position order.

gb1.split_policy: Unassigned. Recommended mutation-depth evaluation: train on Hamming distance <= k from VDGV and test > k (k=1,2,3), deriving depth from input only. These recipes are not official assigned FLIP folds.
gb1.missing_policy: No labels are imputed. Only complete supported structures and finite observed source labels are emitted.
gb1.precision_policy: Candidate keeps parsed source numbers. Release formatter caps all numeric values at 12 significant digits.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.evidence: Original eLife article copyright and license; FLIP README Data licensing confirms original eLife raw data CC BY 4.0. Only original author Mutfit records, not FLIP derivative records, are used.

quality_findings: Exactly 149361 standard four-amino-acid variants have finite observed I20fit and at least 10 input reads.
Missing standard variants are not fabricated or filled from result/regression_missing; that file was not downloaded.
Observed zero fitness is retained. Values below 0.01 are flagged as detection-limit sensitive, without replacing or censoring their numeric labels.
The source uses calibrated earlier experimental single-mutant fitness values; they are measured-derived, not modeled imputations.
Raw counts, alternative fitness values and Hamming distance are excluded from input.
gb1.source_citation: Wu NC, Dai L, Olson CA, Lloyd-Smith JO, Sun R. Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths. eLife 2016;5:e16965. https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.16965
gb1.target_origin: experimental enrichment-derived relative fitness; single substitutions use author-calibrated prior experimental values
gb1.grouping_rule: Exact four-residue variant identity. All samples share one GB1 assay background; identity grouping does not make random splits a cross-protein evaluation.

jdft2d.name: JARVIS 2D / Matbench jdft2d

field_descriptions.lattice_vectors_angstrom: Three lattice vectors as a 3x3 row matrix in angstrom.
field_descriptions.sites: Ordered atomic sites with element symbols and fractional coordinates relative to the lattice. Coordinates outside [0,1) are valid periodic representations.
field_descriptions.periodic: Periodic boundary conditions along all three lattice directions; the slab cell includes vacuum.

jdft2d.split_policy: Unassigned. Use reduced-composition groups for family holdout. These are not official Matbench fivefold assignments and no official benchmark result is claimed.
jdft2d.missing_policy: No labels are imputed. Only complete supported structures and finite observed source labels are emitted.
jdft2d.precision_policy: Candidate keeps parsed source numbers. Release formatter caps all numeric values at 12 significant digits.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.evidence: Original Figshare article 6815705 version 1 API license field.

quality_findings: All 636 labels, lattice matrices, species and fractional coordinates match the original licensed Figshare snapshot row by row.
Only lattice, full-occupancy species, fractional coordinates and periodic boundary flags are input; DFT energies used to generate the target are excluded.
Coordinates outside the unit interval are valid periodic representations and are retained; no artificial clipping/wrapping is applied.
Composition groups conservatively prevent polymorph/alternative-cell separation; structure equivalence is not separately claimed.
Labels are calculated DFT values and inputs are relaxed source geometries; this is not an experimental or raw pre-DFT-geometry benchmark.
jdft2d.source_citation: Choudhary K et al. (2017), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-05402-0. JARVIS 2D snapshot jdft_2d-7-7-2018.json v1, https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.6815705.v1. Matbench structure/exfoliation_en packaging by the Matbench/matminer authors.

cmapss.name: NASA C-MAPSS turbofan degradation

license.attribution: NASA Ames Prognostics Center of Excellence; A. Saxena, K. Goebel, D. Simon and N. Eklund (2008).

cmapss.source_citation: A. Saxena, K. Goebel, D. Simon and N. Eklund (2008). Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation. PHM08. Dataset DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15346912.
cmapss.field_descriptions: history_columns defines each of the 30 chronological history rows: cycle (operating cycles), three operational settings, and sensor_1 through sensor_21. Sensor and setting values retain original published scales; individual physical units are unspecified in the source readme. subset identifies the published operating-condition/fault scenario. No engine ID is an input feature.
cmapss.grouping_rule: One group per published subset, official split and engine; overlapping windows from one engine remain together. Train and test unit numbers are separate engines.
cmapss.split_policy: Original train/test membership is preserved. No validation split is fitted or assigned. Future validation must reserve whole training engines; never randomly split overlapping windows. Official test engines with fewer than 30 cycles are excluded and enumerated.

sampling.train_endpoint_rule: 30,40,... plus each engine final cycle exactly once
sampling.test_endpoint_rule: one official endpoint per eligible engine

quality_findings: Synthetic simulation with sensor noise; no real-engine generalization is established.
RUL is derived from train failure time and read directly from official endpoint labels for test.
Training histories overlap; all windows of an engine share a group.
The source readme final-column sensor26 typo is resolved from the 26-column schema: 2 identifiers + 3 settings + 21 sensors.
The source readme FD004 train/test engine counts are reversed: full-file counts are 249 train and 248 test; actual aggregate counts are 709 train and 707 test.
No scaling, missing-value imputation, RUL cap, or training was performed.

camels_gb.name: CAMELS-GB v1 next-day specific discharge

attribution: Contains data supplied by UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology.
Copyright UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology.
Contains Environment Agency information, copyright Environment Agency and/or database right.
Derived from UK bedrock hydrogeological mapping and UK superficial productivity mapping, BGS copyright UKRI.

camels_gb.source_citation: Coxon, G.; Addor, N.; Bloomfield, J.P.; Freer, J.; Fry, M.; Hannaford, J.; Howden, N.J.K.; Lane, R.; Lewis, M.; Robinson, E.L.; Wagener, T.; Woods, R. (2020). Catchment attributes and hydro-meteorological timeseries for 671 catchments across Great Britain (CAMELS-GB). NERC Environmental Information Data Centre. https://doi.org/10.5285/8344e4f3-d2ea-44f5-8afa-86d2987543a9
camels_gb.source_row_policy: All original daily rows are retained unchanged in the raw archive. Monthly forecast opportunities are selected or excluded; exclusion counts are candidate windows, not original rows.
camels_gb.field_descriptions: history_columns defines seven chronological daily records. precipitation and potential_evapotranspiration use mm/day; temperature uses degrees Celsius; discharge uses mm/day. The last history date is one day before forecast_origin_date, providing a conservative availability lag for water-day/calendar-day conventions. target_date is the following date after the forecast origin. Static inputs are catchment area (km^2), gauge elevation (m above sea level), latitude/longitude (degrees); null means an unavailable static attribute. No catchment identifier, full-period hydrological statistic, or target-day weather is an input.
camels_gb.grouping_rule: One group per catchment ID. Catchment IDs are provenance only. Groups are not asserted to be spatially independent; nested/nearby catchments may be correlated.
camels_gb.split_policy: Unassigned. For future-time validation, divide by target date and require every history date to remain before its target; reserve a gap of at least 8 days at boundaries. For unseen-catchment evaluation reserve whole catchments and preferably whole river basins/spatial regions. No random row splitting.

sampling.forecast_origins: every calendar month-end in the complete published 1970-10-01 to 2015-09-30 period
sampling.reason: Cover all catchments and all years while limiting near-repeated prompts and source size; this is a deterministic monthly subsample of daily forecasting opportunities, not all daily rows.
sampling.missing_policy: Exclude missing/nonfinite or negative discharge label; exclude incomplete histories; never impute; preserve missing static attributes as null.

quality_findings: Monthly origins are sampled; this does not support unbiased daily-event or flood-frequency evaluation.
Rainfall labelled d may aggregate 09:00 d to 09:00 d+1; NRFA flows may use water days or calendar days. The one-day history lag prevents overlap with the next-day target for these conventions.
Retrospectively revised and spatially processed meteorological archives do not establish real-time operational availability.
Only topographic area and gauge coordinates/elevation are selected; full-period q_mean, runoff ratio, flow quantiles and climate summaries are excluded.
Missing discharge is not zero. Zero flow is retained.
Label is the published discharge_spec in mm/day, not an invented conversion from discharge_vol.
Catchment boundary and flow observation uncertainties remain; neighboring/nested catchments are not independent.
No normalization, imputation, model fitting or training was performed.
